summary: Circuit-breaker snapshot & rollback guidance for oscillating tail-latency after adaptive prefetch + quant profile change
description:
Issue summary: After applying an adaptive prefetch + quantization profile to BrightHealth AI's tenant in Dedicated, a subset of requests began showing oscillating tail-latency spikes (~95-99p) and occasional client disconnects. Customer wants prescriptive steps to safely engage a circuit-breaker, restore a known-good snapshot for their tenant, and confirm post-rollback validation criteria.

Context: The tenant was part of a controlled optimizer experiment targeting lower token cost using aggressive KV-prefetch and mixed-precision quant profiles. The change was deployed via the console's optimizer rollout on 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Suspected interaction between prefetch eviction behavior and quantized kernels causing intermittent token-processing stalls on some GPUs.
impact: Intermittent but customer-visible: higher 95/99th latency (from ~180ms -> 700-1200ms) and ~0.8% increase in stream disconnects for the tenant. Traffic is dedicated; no cross-tenant bleed reported. Business impact: feature latency regressions affecting user-facing chat sessions and increased error rate for health triage flows. Customer requested urgent rollback guidance and temporary traffic mitigation steps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant traffic profile: 40% short-chat (mean 32 tokens), 60% long-chat (mean 240 tokens).
2) Applied optimizer profile: kv-prefetch=true, prefetch_eviction=aggressive, quant_profile=mixed-int8-fp16, async_batching=on at 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC via Console rollout pane.
3) Observe production traces and 95/99th latency increase on us-east serving hosts for model gpt-open-13b-quant-v2 between 2026-03-10 02:00-05:00 UTC.
4) Reproduce in canary: run tenant replay for a 2-hour window with same traffic mix against the optimized profile to surface tail behavior.
observed_logs: [2026-03-10T02:13:18Z] host-gpu-14 kernel stall detected - kv-evict loop entered repeatedly (trace id: 8bf3c6)
[2026-03-10T02:13:19Z] streaming connection closed by server (code=1006) - client session id abcd-1234
[2026-03-10T02:45:02Z] quant-kernel-fallback triggered for shard s3 on host-gpu-20; processing latency increased
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive prefetch eviction combined with mixed-int8 kernel selection is causing cache churn and occasional kernel fallback which manifests as tail spikes.
Telemetry shows correlated CPU runnable stalls on hosts that served long sequence requests; nodes with older CUDA drivers are seeing more frequent kernel fallback events.
Canary replay reproduces p99 spikes when prefetch_eviction=aggressive and quant_profile=mixed-int8-fp16, but not when prefetch_eviction=balanced.
Related metric: kv_cache_eviction_rate for tenant increased 6x post-rollout; batch composition shifted slightly toward longer sequences which worsens impact.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10): Logged after customer reported 95/99 latency regressions. Attached their tenant id and console rollout id. Asked for urgent mitigation plan.
Diego Alvarez (2026-03-10): Investigating. Requested traces, a sample pcap of requests, and Prometheus exporters for the affected hosts. Kicked off a canary replay job (replay id: replay-9237).

SRE - Priya Nair (2026-03-11): Observed kernel fallback logs on host-gpu-20 & host-gpu-14. Suggested temporary circuit-breaker to redirect 50% of traffic to pinned non-quant model variant while restoring tenant snapshot.
Customer - BrightHealth Support (2026-03-11): Agrees to traffic split for immediate relief. Asks for step-by-step rollback that doesn't require a full offboard.
Diego Alvarez (2026-03-12): Drafted stepwise plan below and requested Approval to execute during low-traffic window (US morning).
recommended_runbook: Step A - Immediate mitigation (circuit-breaker + traffic split):

1) In Console -> Traffic Routing, create a soft circuit-breaker rule for tenant brighthealth-ai to route 50% of requests to model=gpt-open-13b (non-quant pinned) and 50% remain on current variant. This reduces exposure while keeping throughput stable.
2) Monitor p95/p99 and stream disconnects for 15 minutes. If p99 falls by >=40%, continue to Step B.
Step B - Snapshot restore for tenant optimizer state:
1) Take a new snapshot of current optimizer settings (snapshot id will be recorded).
2) Restore the tenant to the last-known-good snapshot dated 2026-03-07-03:12 (snap-20260307-0312) using Console -> Tenant Snapshots -> Restore (choose 'tenant-only' scope).
3) After restore, ensure kv_prefetch=false or prefetch_eviction=balanced (confirm via API GET /v1/tenants/{id}/optimizer-config).
4) Revert quant_profile to mixed-fp16 (non-int8) for the tenant if snapshot doesn't already contain it.
Step C - Validation and graduated re-enable:
1) Run a focused canary replay for 30 minutes against the restored config and confirm p50/p95/p99 latency and no increase in stream disconnects.
2) If stable, route traffic back in 25% increments every 10 minutes from pinned model -> optimized model while monitoring.
- If p99 remains >500ms after Step A, escalate to a full traffic switch to pinned model (100%).
- If disconnect rate increases after snapshot restore, open INC and pause further changes.
rollback_actions_taken: 2026-03-12 09:15 UTC: Created circuit-breaker rule and routed 50% traffic to non-quant pinned model (gpt-open-13b) as a soft mitigate.
2026-03-12 09:35 UTC: Observed p99 drop from ~1100ms -> ~260ms for tenant traffic. Stream disconnects down to baseline.
2026-03-12 10:05 UTC: Restored snapshot snap-20260307-0312 for tenant optimizer config and set prefetch_eviction=balanced, quant_profile=mixed-fp16.
2026-03-12 10:40 UTC: Canary replay showed stable p99 ~210-300ms for 30 minutes. Began 25% traffic re-merge at 10:45 UTC.
resolution: Mitigation successful. Circuit-breaker + snapshot restore stabilized tail latency and eliminated elevated disconnects. Customer confirmed acceptance of restored optimizer profile and requested a follow-up postmortem and guidance for safer experiments (gradual rollouts, preflight replays). Next steps: SRE/Runtime to add a pre-deploy check for quant-kernel compatibility matrix for nodes with older drivers; Product to add a tenant-level 'experiment guard' that automatically suggests lower prefetch aggressiveness for long-sequence-heavy workloads.
follow_up_actions: SRE: Add a preflight check that flags nodes with CUDA driver < 12.1 when mixed-int8 quant profiles are requested.
Runtime: Add a throttled-prefetch mode that reduces eviction aggressiveness when median sequence length > 128.
Support: Schedule joint postmortem with BrightHealth and provide experiment checklist template.
Product: Expose a one-click safe-rollback that bundles snapshot restore + traffic split in Console.
